Below is one possible fix that treats the function‐capture operator (`&foo?/2`, `&bar!/1`, etc.) as its own token before the generic “slash‐as‐regex” rule ever fires. By inserting a small mode into `ELIXIR_DEFAULT_CONTAINS` we “eat” the `&name/arity` pattern so the `/` will no longer be seen as the start of a regexp.

    // recognize Elixir function captures like &foo?/1 or &Bar!/2

      relevance: 0

What this does:

- We add a mode that matches `&` followed by a valid Elixir identifier (with optional `?`, `!`, or `=` at the end) then a slash and one or more digits.
- Because this mode appears *before* the big regexp‐container rule, the `/` in `&letter?/1` is no longer picked up as the start of a JavaScript‐style regexp literal.
- Highlight.js will render `&letter?/1` in one piece (unstyled or with your chosen `meta` style) and continue coloring the rest of the line correctly.
